title: The Nilgiri Loop
tagline: Bangalore → Dimbam ghat → Kotagiri → Coonoor → Ooty → Gudalur → Mudumalai → Bandipur → Bangalore. 610 km, two tiger reserves and a 27-hairpin climb.
summary: A clockwise loop out of Bangalore that climbs into the Nilgiris the hard way — up the Dimbam ghat from the Sathyamangalam forests — rides the tea-estate ridge from Kotagiri to Ooty, drops through Gudalur, and comes home along the Mudumalai–Bandipur elephant corridor. Doable as a very long single day (14–16 hours of riding) but far better as two days with a night in Coonoor or Ooty.

credit.name: @odesseyofduo_4.9.25 & @sheidu_khan on Instagram
credit.note: the 'Nilgiri Loop' reel that started this entry — 610 km, 27 hairpins (yes, they counted)

segments.road: NH 948 via Kanakapura → Malavalli → Kollegal → Chamarajanagar → Sathyamangalam road
segments.note: Fast, mostly two-lane. Fuel up at Chamarajanagar. The last 30 km before Dimbam run through Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve.
The 27 hairpins are on the Dimbam climb. Narrow, blind corners, buses cutting the apex. Then rolling plateau to Kotagiri.
Tea estates both sides; stop at the Kotagiri view points. Foggy after noon.
Runs beside the Nilgiri Mountain Railway. Heavy tourist traffic on weekends.
Long descent, some broken patches after monsoon. Pykara falls and Naduvattam viewpoint en route.
Enter Mudumalai Tiger Reserve. 40 km/h, no stopping, no horn.
Elephant corridor; the most likely stretch for an elephant on the road.

segments.road: Bandipur → Gundlupet → Mysore ring road → NH 275 Bangalore
segments.note: Clear Bandipur before the two-wheeler cut-off. The Mysore–Bangalore expressway is fast and dull.

highlights: The Dimbam climb — 27 numbered hairpins rising out of the Sathyamangalam forest with the plains behind you.
Kotagiri to Coonoor ridge road through tea estates; Kodanad and Catherine Falls viewpoints are short detours.
Coonoor–Ooty alongside the toy train line; Lamb's Rock and Dolphin's Nose near Coonoor.
Pykara Falls and the Naduvattam viewpoint on the Ooty–Gudalur descent.
Mudumalai and Bandipur — riding through two tiger reserves back-to-back, elephants and gaur likely at dusk.

offroad.summary: This is a tarmac loop — the challenge is the ghat sections, not dirt. Any road bike handles it; an ADV or scrambler just makes the broken patches easier.
notes: Dimbam ghat: tight hairpins with loose gravel on the inside line after rain. Keep to your lane — buses use the whole road.
Ooty–Gudalur descent has potholed stretches and washed-out edges after the monsoon (Jun–Sep). Ride in the tyre tracks.
Optional dirt detour: the Masinagudi–Ooty 'Kalhatti ghat' (36 hairpins, very steep, one lane) instead of Gudalur — only in dry weather and only if you're confident with steep low-speed hairpins.
Fog and wet roads in Coonoor/Ooty from mid-afternoon; moss on the shaded corners is slippery.
Luggage: soft panniers or a tail bag; hard cases make the hairpin lane-share with buses tighter than you'd like.

timings: Bandipur & Mudumalai forest stretch is CLOSED to all traffic 9:00 PM – 6:00 AM every day (Karnataka HC order). Two-wheelers are restricted earlier on the Bandipur side, roughly from 6:00 PM — plan to clear Bandipur by late afternoon.
Sathyamangalam forest (before Dimbam) has check posts; night riding is discouraged and elephants cross the road.
No permits needed. Carry ID; forest check posts may ask.
Fuel: Chamarajanagar and Sathyamangalam before the climb; Kotagiri, Coonoor, Ooty, Gudalur on the plateau; Gundlupet after Bandipur. Nothing inside the reserves.
cautions: Wild elephants on the road in Sathyamangalam, Mudumalai and Bandipur — stop, kill the engine, give way, never overtake a herd.
Ooty–Coonoor weekend traffic can add an hour; start the loop before 5 AM if attempting it in one day.
Cold: Ooty drops to single digits in Dec–Jan mornings. Layers and a neck gaiter.
The 14–16 hour figure is riding time only. Two riders in the source reel did it; most people should split it.
